- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.18) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior period), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +3% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is positive (≥0.36) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 1–2% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.18–0.36), model often underestimates mean reversion; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias to align with historical mean.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to lag by 1–2 days in reaction to sentiment shifts; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- If sentiment turns negative after a peak, model often fails to anticipate sharp drop; reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is high and price is near support, model often ignores support; add 0.5–1.5% downward bias to prevent overextension.
